package_info.why_malicious: The provided report is a general overview of software supply chain attack techniques (dependency confusion, typosquatting, brandjacking, malicious code injection) and best practices for defense. It does not analyze or describe any specific malicious package or code sample. Therefore, no concrete package-level metadata or macro-level malicious assessment can be extracted.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected package versions with abnormally high numbers (dependency confusion)
Packages with names similar to popular components (typosquatting/brandjacking)
Code changes in open source libraries that introduce obfuscated or suspicious logic (malicious code injection)
file_indicators: Packages with names differing by a single character from popular libraries
Packages published with unusually high version numbers
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound network requests from build or install scripts
Connections to domains not associated with the legitimate package
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation of packages with suspiciously high version numbers or names similar to popular libraries. Scan for unexpected network activity during package installation or build processes. Review code changes in dependencies for obfuscated or unauthorized logic. Use SBOMs and automated tools to identify and quarantine suspicious or unverified components before they enter the development pipeline.
